Synthetic panel of women's weekly earnings

Source: R/data.R
earnings_panel.Rd

A simulated two-wave panel of women's weekly earnings, used to demonstrate the descriptive and causal variance decompositions. Its structure and variable names follow the Current Population Survey (CPS): each woman is observed in two consecutive years, and some women (mother = 1) have their first child between the two waves. All values are simulated; no real survey records are included.

Usage

data(earnings_panel)

Format

A data frame with 15,200 rows (7,600 women x 2 waves) and 12 variables:

id

Person identifier.

year

Survey year (1982–2020).

decade

Decade of the first wave (1980, 1990, 2000, 2010); the same for both waves of a person.

post

Wave indicator: 0 = first wave, 1 = second wave (after the birth, for mothers).

mother

1 if the woman has her first child between the two waves, 0 otherwise.

earnweek

Weekly earnings in dollars (0 if not employed).

earnwt

Earnings weight.

educ

Education: factor with levels "HS or less", "Some college", "BA+".

ses

Socioeconomic status: factor with levels "Low", "Middle", "High".

age

Age in years.

race

Race/ethnicity: factor with levels "White", "Black", "Hispanic", "Other".

married

1 if married, 0 otherwise.

Details

The data-generating process is stylized: motherhood lowers employment and mean earnings and raises earnings dispersion, more so for less-educated women, and these penalties shrink over time; the share of mothers falls, the share with a BA rises, and within-group dispersion grows. Draws are stratified so that results are smooth despite the modest sample size. See create/create_earnings_panel.R in the package source for the full data-generating process.

Examples

data(earnings_panel)
head(earnings_panel)
#>   id year decade post mother earnweek earnwt       educ ses age  race married
#> 1  1 1982   1980    0      0   263.81   2846 HS or less Low  40 White       1
#> 2  1 1983   1980    1      0     0.00   2846 HS or less Low  41 White       1
#> 3  2 1982   1980    0      0     0.00   3108 HS or less Low  24 White       1
#> 4  2 1983   1980    1      0     0.00   3108 HS or less Low  25 White       1
#> 5  3 1982   1980    0      0     0.00   2395 HS or less Low  24 White       0
#> 6  3 1983   1980    1      0     0.00   2395 HS or less Low  25 White       0
